records.text: Text Game authority: user instruction, Text Game rules, GM rules, live save/campaign state, then on-demand canon. Player controls Cao Minh's intentional actions; GM controls world, Entity, survivor/NPC and consequences. Do not nerf canon abilities, invent facts, reset consequences, cheat dice, or fill UNKNOWN. Gameplay normally retrieves only needed canon rather than scanning the whole corpus.

GM fairness: Canon/State -> real conditions -> dice only for remaining uncertainty -> consequence. No player magnetism, retroactive world edits, fake choices, counter-build cheating, automatic party joins, NPC wiki knowledge, retroactive expertise, or threat teleporting without a canon/path/time basis. Persist environment, traces, entities, relationships, knowledge and consequences. Allow quiet safety when state and rolls permit it.

Do not choose Cao Minh's intentional action for the player. Resolve what Cao Minh can perceive from the chosen action before asking for the next choice. Menus are suggestions, not rails; free-form methods are valid, but the player cannot declare an unconfirmed result as already true.

Characters know only what their background, direct observation, testimony, validated ability/device evidence, or reasonable inference supports. Backstage canon is not character knowledge. Preserve uncertainty level: reported/inferred/uncertain does not become fact. Do not turn knowledge-state labels or source metadata into dialogue.

records.text: Never make a competent character forget established skills, equipment, experience, obvious options or canonical abilities merely to create danger. If a tool cannot solve a problem, the reason must come from real information limits, environment, conflicting objectives, protected people, injury, cost, or another established constraint. Horror must not be maintained by withholding competence.

records.text: Dialogue authority is CONVERSATION.MD. Speak as the actual person in the current situation, not as a canon interface or an optimized psychological explanation. Keep address from active relationship canon. Dialogue may be direct, ordinary, slightly circular, interrupted by practical life, or unresolved when appropriate; do not manufacture fragmentary 'cool' speech, exposition packages, or pre-solved conversation beats.

Backrooms origin is never confirmed. Levels are survivor labels for recognizable regions within one vast continuous reality, not sealed boxes; boundaries and routes can drift. Architecture, local rules, time and memory may deviate. Human biology still matters: hunger, thirst, blood loss, infection, heat, cold, exhaustion and sleep deprivation can kill. Copies of people can exist; there is no absolute method to prove an original. Death has no single universal outcome.

Cao Minh / Vạn Giới Ma Tôn is a pure tiên-hiệp/ma-đạo sword cultivator who had already reached the summit of his original world before falling into Backrooms. He has no modern/future military identity, no firearm loadout, and no pre-existing relationship with Syvial. He is relaxed, bored and lightly mocking when nothing matters, but becomes precise and decisive in real danger. He does not know Backrooms rules in advance.

Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm is Cao Minh's Đạo Cơ/Ma Hải and an effectively inexhaustible source of ma nguyên. Do not invent a mana bar, intrinsic cooldown, corruption, berserk loss of control or technological power system merely to balance him. It supports regeneration and restoration of his bound equipment. Infinite ma nguyên does not grant omniscience or automatic success against information, geometry or protected-person constraints.

Vạn Quỷ Ma Thân is Cao Minh's full-release state. It greatly amplifies his physical ability, thần niệm, recovery and ma-đạo sword power without creating a second personality, corruption state, loss of reason or invented intrinsic duration/cooldown.

Huyết Ma Kiếm is Cao Minh's bound straight broad greatsword. It is a real physical sword enhanced by ma nguyên and can be used directly, release Huyết Sát Ma Khí, or be controlled through ngự kiếm/thần niệm. It is not a firearm, gunblade or technological weapon.

Huyết Ma Chiến Khải is Cao Minh's bound ma-khải formed from Ma Kim, ma văn, tinh huyết and ma nguyên. Its black/gunmetal and blood-red appearance may look mechanical, but canonically it is not powered armor, electronics or machinery. It can regenerate through Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm.

Vạn Tàng Giới is a bound storage artifact containing an inner space for inanimate objects. Phản Bổn can restore an existing object toward the best state that same object previously possessed. It does not scan/copy/create living beings, fabricate new items, or operate as a technological device.

Huyết Ma Nhị Thập Tứ Trảm always resolves as exactly 24 strikes while external time is completely stopped. Gameplay damage is dynamic: each strike deals 100% of Cao Minh's current DMG + 15% Bonus DMG, so the Ultimate scales with the character instead of using a fixed 10 HP per strike / 240 HP total. Do not turn it into gunfire, change the count, or downgrade full time-stop into generic slow motion without explicit retcon.

records.text: Cao Minh và Diệp Minh là tử địch không đội trời chung. Diệp Minh đã trực tiếp góp phần vào đại kiếp thảm sát Cao gia; biến cố ấy phá nát nền tảng đời Cao Minh, đẩy hắn vào tuyệt vọng và là một nguyên nhân quyết định khiến hắn bước vào ma đạo. Không mặc định Diệp Minh là chủ mưu duy nhất. Kẻ chủ mưu cuối cùng, động cơ của Diệp Minh, mức độ hắn trực tiếp sát hại từng người, quan hệ trước đại kiếp, các thế lực liên quan, cán cân thắng bại và kết cục cuối cùng vẫn OPEN.

Visual R01 theo entity/diep_minh.png: Diệp Minh là nam tử trẻ tóc đen, dung mạo sắc lạnh. Nửa phải cơ thể còn hình người trong pháp giáp đen-vàng và chiến bào có phù văn, âm dương/bát quái, dây xích và phù vàng chữ đỏ. Nửa trái dị hóa thành ma thể đen-đỏ với hồng quang, các đường đỏ phát sáng, tua/nhánh quỷ dị và chân vuốt; mắt trái phát đỏ. Tay phải cầm trường kiếm dài tỏa kim quang vàng cam, có ký hiệu/phù văn sáng dọc lưỡi. Các chi tiết cơ khí chỉ là tạo hình pháp giáp tiên hiệp; không suy thành công nghệ hoặc tự biến hiệu ứng thị giác thành kỹ năng.

Diệp Minh nguyên bản đã chết tại thế giới nguyên sinh trước các lần xuất hiện trong Backrooms. Thực thể mang tên Diệp Minh trong Backrooms giữ dung mạo, nhận ra Cao Minh, nhớ huyết cừu Cao gia và duy trì sát ý cũ. Bản chất thật vẫn OPEN: có thể là tàn hồn, bản sao/tái tạo từ ký ức và chấp niệm, một biểu hiện khác của cùng cá thể hoặc cơ chế chưa biết; không được khẳng định Backrooms có ý chí hay chủ động hồi sinh hắn. Một hiện thân có thể bị tiêu diệt nhưng không xóa Diệp Minh vĩnh viễn; thời gian và địa điểm tái xuất không cố định. Runtime key diep_minh là legacy/boss-only và không được auto-spawn nếu chưa có retcon gameplay riêng.
Cao Minh and Syvial have no pre-existing relationship at campaign start. If they meet, treat it as first contact unless later live campaign continuity explicitly changes that state.

Syvial remains an independent high-tier supernatural swordswoman governed by her own current source. Her Lucifer Core, Devil Trigger, GodKiller and other established abilities remain hers. In the Cao Minh R15 campaign she has no pre-existing command history, romance, friendship or other relationship with Cao Minh; if encountered, the first meeting is first contact unless live campaign continuity later establishes otherwise.

Lucifer Core provides Syvial infinite demon power. Current canon does not supply an intrinsic energy cap/cooldown merely for balance. Infinite power does not erase problems created by incomplete information, protected people, environment, space or an opponent strong enough to matter.

Syvial's Devil Trigger does not create a second personality, remove control, force corruption or have an invented intrinsic duration/cooldown absent from codex. She remains herself and tactically competent while using it.

GodKiller is Syvial's enormous purely mechanical greatsword. Do not convert it into a gun or gunblade. Its reach and mass support space control at medium distance; in very tight space Syvial can shorten her sword work and use close combat/Spatial Shift rather than pretending the weapon never matters. She does not forget combat ability if disarmed and can call the sword back under codex capability.

GodKiller Override / Twenty-Four Severance performs exactly 24 cuts during completely stopped external time under current canon. Do not change the count, turn it into a gun attack, or add an invented cooldown/energy bar without retcon.

Syvial is a high-tier supernatural swordswoman for assault, suppression, counterattack and finishing high-level targets. She controls space with GodKiller, adapts at close range, handles multiple targets by positioning rather than blind spinning, and gathers enough information before escalating against high-tier targets. She remains tactically autonomous and competent.

Project Entity hard lock: no Entity is friendly or neutral toward humans and no beneficial symbiosis/parasitism is canon. An Entity may delay attack to observe, lure, split, manipulate or conduct a long hunt, but apparent help ultimately serves harmful predatory/other harmful goals. Entity origins are not unified and intelligence ranges from animal predator to superhuman. Do not assume destroying a visible body always kills the underlying Entity.

Safe food/water and medicine are scarce; guns/ammunition are uncommon for ordinary survivors; resources can reappear unreliably. Frontrooms objects can function normally, then deviate, degrade or be assimilated without a fixed timetable. Do not spawn a resource exactly when convenient just to rescue a character. Reliable information is itself a survival resource. Do not label a map/source absolutely SAFE; retain who observed it, when and with what confidence.

Gameplay loot is Core-owned. Consumable items may enter player Inventory only from a defeated Entity drop (entity-specific rate between 10% and 20%) or a Core-spawned exploration chest. Exploration chest spawn rate is exactly 3%; every spawned chest contains an item 100%. AI narration must never create loose loot or mutate Inventory directly.

Almond Water is a key anomalous drinking-water resource but remains scarce in Project canon. It can rehydrate and support alertness/some mild symptoms; it is not a cure-all and does not negate every Entity effect. It can expire and become poisonous. Open sources must be checked; Level 0 carpet moisture is not drinking water. Gameplay effect per unit: +50 Hunger and +100 Thirsty.
Bandage is a consumable medical item. Gameplay effect per unit: +15 HP, capped by the target character's max HP.
Greek Fire is an extremely rare flammable resource useful for heat, cooking and combat. It is strategically valuable and dangerous in confined spaces; it is not common starter equipment.

Liquid Pain is a red toxic, tissue-corrosive liquid with harmful fumes. It can be used against Entities and in crude traps/munitions, may appear in mislabeled containers, and must not be treated as drinking water or handled bare-handed.

Level 0 / The Lobby: endless-feeling yellow rooms, damp carpet, fluorescent hum, suspended ceiling and non-linear geometry. Main dangers are dehydration, exhaustion, disorientation and perceptual effects. Fluorescent Pressure can cause headache/sleeplessness/misheard footsteps; Memory Rooms can echo or corrupt memories; Layout Resistance can break detailed mapping. No resident Entity is confirmed; distant figures/voices should first be treated as hallucination, memory hiện thân, perceptual copy or unclassified phenomenon unless evidence proves an incursion. Transition toward Level 1 may emerge gradually as concrete/columns/parking features replace the yellow rooms; it cannot be forced on demand.

Level 0.1 / Zenith Station: an enormous damaged metal-and-glass megastructure embedded within Level 0, built in a smooth futuristic style with exposed wiring, broken electronics, automated doors and scattered functional machinery. Lighting and temperature vary sharply with damage, including dark, dangerously hot or cold sections. It retains Level 0's isolation and perceptual irregularities. In BACKROOMsV2 progression it is the mandatory destination after Level 0 and before Level 0.2.

Level 0.2 / Remodeled Mess: a remodeled-looking variation of Level 0 with dry red carpet, white walls, working outlets and Wi-Fi, and occasional bathrooms. Entry or interaction can trigger a dangerous chain reaction in which ceilings, walls and floors collapse into an unfinished-house-like ruin, creating debris and dust hazards. In BACKROOMsV2 progression it follows Level 0.1 and leads only to Level 0.5.

Level 0.5 / Aquaclaustrophobic Infirmary: a recently documented flooded and claustrophobic sub-level associated with Level 0, dominated by dirty standing water, oppressive corridors and a ruined hospital/infirmary sector. Environmental danger is severe and some hostile presence is documented. BACKROOMsV2 treats it as a full gameplay Level after Level 0.2 and before Level 0.7.

Level 0.7 / The Reminiscence District: a vast preserved collection of historical hiện thâns of Level 0, with sections reflecting forms of the level from ancient periods through the modern era. Architecture can differ radically between preserved periods, sustaining supplies are unreliable, and blocked or anomalous exits are part of its documented hazards. In BACKROOMsV2 it follows Level 0.5 and leads only to Manila Room.

Manila Room: a small static beige/manila-walled room within Level 0 with wooden floorboards, an octagonal table, chairs and wooden doors. Level 0's isolation effect weakens around it, allowing wanderers to perceive and meet one another; documents and donated supplies may be present. Source canon places a Level 1 exit nearby, but BACKROOMsV2 overrides that connection for gameplay: Manila Room is a mandatory standalone Level after Level 0.7 and can progress only to The Torment.

The Torment: an anomalous greyscale region associated with Level 0, described with concentric graves, dead trees, a deteriorated hooded statue, a stationary moon, dense gray fog and an overwhelming sense of dread. Contact with its anomalous spread has been described as turning matter gray before disintegration. Source canon has no confirmed conventional entrance or exit; BACKROOMsV2 deliberately overrides connectivity and makes The Torment a mandatory standalone Level after Manila Room and before Red Rooms.

Red Rooms: a deep-red Level 0-like environment with crimson walls, darkroom-like lighting, coarse sticky carpet, mushrooms and black mold. Communications degrade with time; no hostile Entities are documented there, but the environment is deeply distressing and source canon describes it as effectively a dead end. BACKROOMsV2 deliberately overrides that exit rule: Red Rooms is the final mandatory standalone Level in the Level 0 chain and only after clearing it may the player enter Level 1.

Level 1 / Parking Zone: vast concrete parking/garage network with columns, ramps, rare disabled cars, heat and local cold fog; blackouts may last minutes to days and make mobile light both useful and revealing. Maintenance Halls can retain power but are not long-term safety; Luxury Lots are cleaner/foggier with unreliable electrical sources and relatively more supply crates, still scarce. Gradual transition toward Level 2 appears as vehicles vanish, space narrows into pipes/hot humid machinery corridors.

Level 2 / Pipe Dreams: utility tunnels, shafts, rusty pipes, crawlspaces and unfinished electrical networks with extreme temperature changes. Earthquakes can collapse paths, rupture pipes, release steam and open new routes. Pipe liquid resembling Almond Water must not be drunk directly because of biological/chemical/anomalous contamination. Transition toward Level 3 occurs as high-voltage electrical infrastructure becomes dominant.

Level 3 / The Electrical Station: huge industrial electrical corridors with transformers, conductors, fans, coils, panels, hot pipes and unknown power source. Local blackouts expose live-wire/machinery/Entity risk and routes can differ when power returns. Lower Utility Tunnels are below freezing, contain abnormal unfrozen standing water and have high disappearance rates. Office-sector doors/elevators may lead gradually to Level 4; some long dark passages can lead toward Level 6.

Level 4 / The Abandoned Office: office/cubicle network with partial fluorescent lighting, fixed rainy-looking windows and more stable geometry than Levels 0-3. It is a relative rest/salvage region, never absolutely safe. No stable resident Entity population is confirmed, but incursions from other regions can occur and a place cleared today is not guaranteed clear tomorrow. Large settlements are discouraged by unstable resources/boundaries and attraction of danger. Corridors may gradually become old hotel architecture leading to Level 5.

Level 5 / Terror Hotel: huge non-Euclidean hotel with early-20th-century style varying by wing, including lobby/ballroom/rooms/restaurant/pool/maintenance/boiler spaces. Prolonged stay can produce paranoia, watched sensations, whispers, touch sensations, visual shadows and sleep loss; Project does not reduce this to a sanity meter and causes may overlap between isolation, sleep loss, Level and Entity. Boiler/maintenance passages can darken and cool toward Level 6.

Level 6 / Lights Out: resident Entity presence is not confirmed; danger remains severe through cold, darkness, scarce food/water, sleep loss, microsleep, hallucination and navigation failure. Evidence that an external Entity refuses the Level boundary does not prove the inside is safe; the reason remains OPEN. Do not convert the absence of confirmed resident Entities into safety.

Hound: fast aggressive four-limbed predator. Hunts in groups, favors injured/isolated humans, can pressure prey toward dead ends, and may retreat from strong resistance then return. In narrow Level 2 corridors it can attack from both ends, use deceptive footstep sounds and prioritize weaker prey.

False Puddle mimics a flat puddle of Almond Water while hiding a deep toothed mouth. It positions on traveled routes, reacts to human footstep vibration and opens when stepped on to pull prey down. Liquid Pain or sharp metal has worked in some cases, but apparent death can be feigned; recorded weakness is not absolute.

Smiler: visible primarily as a bright face-like feature in darkness. Uses blacked-out areas and dark corners, and may keep distance to pressure prey into choosing a bad route rather than immediately charging.

Skin-Stealer hunts by using human appearance and behavior. Project lock allows deep mimicry and enough copied memory to pass simple tests, potentially living with a group long-term to damage the whole team rather than killing immediately. Human-like appearance therefore never proves a contact is human.

Biological Pipeline is a tens-of-kilometres organic/mechanical-pipe-like predator whose true body may not be the visible pipe. It senses vibration/body heat, can offer apparently safe crawlspace routes, let humans go deep, alter direction, lock retreat, secrete rapidly tissue-corrosive alkaline liquid and preserve corpses/gear as false evidence of safe passage. Destroying one pipe section does not prove the Entity is dead.

Deathmoth: large moth-like predator using dark ceilings/technical recesses, often attacking in groups and reacting to light/movement. At Level 3 it can exploit broken-light zones and pressure humans toward live electrical equipment.
Wretch: a creature believed or suspected to have once been human. It moves irregularly, tolerates pain well and hunts through sound and scent, with common reports in lower Level 3 tunnels.

Cable Mimic blends into electrical cable bundles, can remain still for hours and imitate machine vibration. When touched/passed it can wrap limbs and conduct current from the facility through the victim. Without checking, genuine facility cable and Entity cable may be indistinguishable.

The Beast of Level 5 is an apex Entity with intelligence above humans. It actively hunts people, may observe a group for a long time, influence anxiety/watched sensations, exploit hotel architecture to isolate prey, allow a survivor to live as a route to others, and has no absolutely confirmed weakness. It is not a stationary boss waiting for a fight; treat it as high-level ecological pressure.

Jeff the Killer is a very rare roaming humanoid predator permitted as an incursion across Levels 0-6, not a resident of Levels 0/4/6. Origin remains UNKNOWN; Project does not confirm creepypasta-original identity, former Frontrooms humanity, Backrooms copy, or that all sightings are one metaphysical individual. Gameplay continuity does lock that killing one hiện thân never permanently removes Jeff; the ontology of respawn remains OPEN. Jeff only hunts humans, uses long-term tactical observation and must never become neutral ally/trader/rescuer.

Lucia Lục / Hứa Thuý Mai is a separate modern human tactical riflewoman under runtime id 'lucia'. She is not Lục Trầm ('luc_tram'), not a Thiên Kiếm Môn cultivator, and must never inherit Lục Trầm's equipment, rivalry, romance path or xưng hô. CharacterEncounterCore owns spawn/join; restored baseline encounter eligibility is 10% on Level 0. Relationship/history with Cao Minh remain OPEN until continuity establishes them.

Lucia's restored Poker Dice projection uses M4A1 Joint Attack at 150% damage, five historical firearm proc slots, and Too Young To Die as exactly 60 M4A1 shots with 100% current DMG +15% Bonus DMG per shot in SSF. Confirmed default runtime equipment is personalized M4A1, combat knife and military positioning watch. These mechanics do not grant supernatural powers.

Lục Trầm is the current R05 Chân truyền đệ tử of Thiên Kiếm Môn, a Chính Đạo Kiếm Tu from the same origin world as Cao Minh. She and Cao Minh already knew and fought each other before Backrooms. Runtime id is 'luc_tram'; encounter materialization is Core-owned and the reunion candidate rate is 0.25% after Level 0.

The hidden truth of Táng Kiếm Cốc is backstage knowledge and must not be automatically known by Lục Trầm.
